text: God, I love it. Good to see you. >> Summer. How's the spring? >> Spring outstanding. Incredible. Kind of limits you, but it really forces to me a coach to think about, okay, how can I maximize this time with a player? And I think this time of year, you get a chance to work with individuals and try to build players and make guys better, which I think is hard to do in the season. It's more about big picture. The next game against this opponent, this is what we're going to have to do. Um, and I think this time of year, it's more about the individual player. And I know that was due to the new kickoff rule, but how much more of an emphasis is there on finding the right kick returners given the, you know, sort of reemergence of that position, I guess. Uh, which is fun. Um, but finding the returner, yeah, obviously to me the returner is going to be crucial. I mean, um, at that position, those guys are touching the ball quite a bit. I would say he's had kind of a Well, I don't think he's ever been a full-time all the time guy back there um the last couple years. I would say he's probably similar to Khalif, right? The fact that he actually contributed on offense, like those guys had scheme plays for him. Um, they wanted him out there to run certain routes and do certain things. That's a lot of value. He returned a lot of balls. A lot of balls he returned. people with fair catch. Um and uh yeah, zero turnovers uh during his time here. Um so great player, did a lot for us. Uh Dorsch obviously excited to have him. He's similar type of player. I think he's coming in with zero touchdowns um on his career. I think his average a little bit less than what Leaf was when he came here. Um and so an opportunity for him to grow and and uh compete. I remember Dorsch when he was at Wake Forest. I think I was at Philly at the time and I was evaluating him um as a player and he was a down the line guy. Wasn't one of the top guys early pick in the draft, but he was a down the line guy and I remember thinking, man, I think this guy's got something in him, you know. Um and then they brought his name up to me obviously this off season. And uh to me, I'm excited about having him and a chance for a guy to uh get a shot to compete and get better and improve, be around some good players that'll help him out. And uh so it should be exciting. We'll see. A >> lot of times uh first year players, rookies that they're they're quickest way onto the field is sometimes, you know, on special teams. I was just curious when you look at the class overall. There looks like some guys that at least, you know, on tape really did some nice things on special teams. You excited about what some of those first year guys may contribute on special teams? >> Yeah. Um you know, the great thing about one of the great things about this business to me, especially in my job, is like the roster flips over every year. It's a brand new start. a lot of new players. Um, and during my time here, we've lost some really good players. Um, and then we've just kind of reloaded and found a way to do that. Um, but, uh, yeah, this class coming in, a bunch of these guys have done some things and then I think some people think these guys have done more than they have. You know, like RER played 13 punts, that's it. So, if he's playing on our punt team this year, he's going to play a lot more than that. Like for Khif Raymond, he came in here one way. I think he left a different way. Um, and I think that it wasn't just me. Obviously, a part of that. Most of it was him and the guys he's around. But to me, that's the exciting thing. Can you build something better um as a team than you had as an individual coming in here? Um, so I think these guys have talent. Coach, >> you guys have kind of been like a model of consistency. You look at you guys have during practices. It's kind of been going the same way. Now maybe there's like, yeah, did we have a rookie mini camp? No. Um, what's that do for me? At the end of the day, this job is about getting certain results. And if you don't get them, it doesn't matter what you do. And then you just say, "How am I going to get the job done with that time that they're giving me?" And don't worry about I missed this or I didn't have that or we're shifting to the n doesn't matter. >> Also, kick rule. I I know it's early, but what kind of growth have you seen from uh Vaky and now from your perspective um him entering and players entering their third year? From your perspective, what kind of things you look for from third year players? >> Yeah. Um I don't know that I look for anything different from third year to first year. But uh in terms of Vaky, I mean, Vaky is he's a very good special teams player. I'll say it that way. As a as a running back, he's as good as any running back I've been around um playing that position or playing on special teams. And uh I'm obviously excited about him. I you know the big thing for him is he's got to stay healthy. You know, he got hurt a little bit last year. Um that didn't help us out. Um but he's got to stay healthy. Other than that, I mean, this guy's a very talented player. He's explosive, great athlete, great guy. I think he works hard. I think he's passionate player, wants to do well uh for the team, and certainly excited to have him here. You >> mentioned, you mentioned the new rules. This is more This is more >> We're going all day. >> Only get one shot. >> You mentioned the new rules. This is more a leaguewide. Do Do you and other special team coaches ever get together and say, "What's the deal with the the on-site kick where you have to tell them that you're going to do it?" >> Yeah. Not to cut you off, but just in terms of all that. So, I I don't ever really get involved with the rules and the whole special teams. Let's get together in a group. That stuff's not for me. Um, so, um, obviously, if a guy hasn't played on punt, that doesn't mean he can't play on punt. uh just means he hasn't been asked to do that.
